Acme Corporation
 Engineering — Production Incident Response Runbook
 Document ID: ACME-ENG-RB-021  |  Version: 4.0  |  Effective Date: February 1, 2026  |  Classification: Internal Use
 Only
1. Purpose
This runbook defines how the Engineering on-call rotation detects, triages, escalates, and resolves
production incidents affecting Acme's customer-facing services. It complements but does not replace the
Information Security Incident Reporting process defined in the IT Security Policy (ACME-POL-IT-014) for
incidents with a security or data-exposure component.
2. Severity Levels and Response Targets
Production incidents are classified SEV1 through SEV4. Response and mitigation targets below apply to
engineering on-call response, which is distinct from the Security Operations Center's security incident
response times.

3. On-Call Escalation Path
 Primary on-call engineer is paged automatically via PagerDuty when an alert fires or a SEV1/SEV2 is
manually declared in #incidents.
 If unacknowledged within the target window, PagerDuty auto-escalates to the secondary on-call
engineer.
 For SEV1 incidents, the Incident Commander role is activated automatically and a dedicated Zoom
bridge and #incident- Slack channel are created.
 If the incident involves suspected unauthorized access, data exfiltration, or a security control failure,
the on-call engineer must also notify the Security Operations Center (SOC) immediately per the IT

the on-call engineer must also notify the Security Operations Center (SOC) immediately per the IT
Security Policy — this triggers the separate, higher-priority security response track.
4. Roles During an Incident

Role
Responsibility
Incident Commander (IC)
Owns overall coordination and external communication decisions
Primary On-Call
Leads technical investigation and mitigation
Scribe
Maintains the incident timeline in the incident channel
Comms Lead
Drafts status page updates and customer-facing communication

5. Status Page and Customer Communication
SEV1 and SEV2 incidents require a status page update within 15 minutes of declaration, with follow-up
updates at least every 30 minutes until resolution. The Comms Lead is responsible for review by a
Director-level approver before any update referencing customer data impact is published.
6. Postmortem Requirements
All SEV1 and SEV2 incidents require a blameless postmortem document published within 5 business days
of resolution, including a timeline, root cause analysis, and at least one concrete follow-up action with an
owner and due date. Postmortems are reviewed in the weekly Engineering Reliability sync and archived in
the Incident Postmortems space in Confluence.
7. Relationship to Security Incident Response
This runbook governs operational/availability incidents. Any incident involving a suspected security breach,
unauthorized access, malware, or exposure of Confidential or Restricted data must be handled under the

unauthorized access, malware, or exposure of Confidential or Restricted data must be handled under the
Information Security Incident Reporting process in the IT Security Policy (ACME-POL-IT-014, Section 5),
which specifies a 15-minute response target for critical security incidents. On-call engineers should treat
that target as the operative one whenever a security dimension is identified, even if this runbook's SEV
classification would otherwise suggest a longer window.
This document is classified Internal Use Only. For questions, contact the Engineering Reliability team at
reliability@acmecorp-internal.example.

1. Purpose
This policy governs how Acme employees request, approve, and report business expenses and how
purchases of goods and services are procured on behalf of the company.

3. Travel Expense Guidelines
 Airfare must be booked in economy class for flights under 6 hours; premium economy is permitted for
flights over 6 hours with director approval.
 Hotel expenses are reimbursed up to $275 per night in major metro areas and $180 per night

flights over 6 hours with director approval.
 Hotel expenses are reimbursed up to $275 per night in major metro areas and $180 per night
elsewhere, receipts required for all amounts.
 Meal per diem is $75 per day domestic and $95 per day international, itemized receipts not required
under $25.
 Ground transportation should default to public transit or rideshare economy tiers; luxury rideshare
tiers are not reimbursable.
4. Corporate Card Policy
Employees with a recurring business travel need may request a corporate card through Finance Ops. All
corporate card transactions must be reconciled in the Expensify system within 15 calendar days of the
transaction date. Cards not reconciled within 45 days are automatically suspended pending manager
review.

5. Software and SaaS Procurement
All new software purchases, including free-tier signups that may later convert to paid plans, must be
logged in the Software Asset Registry and reviewed by IT Security for data handling and vendor risk before
purchase, regardless of dollar amount. This applies in addition to, not instead of, the standard expense
approval thresholds in Section 2. Procurement of any tool that will process Confidential or Restricted data
(as classified in the IT Security Policy, ACME-POL-IT-014) requires a completed vendor security
questionnaire prior to approval.
6. Prohibited Expenses
 Personal entertainment, gym memberships, or spa services.
 Alcohol at a value exceeding $50 per event when client entertainment is involved.
 Traffic violations, parking tickets, or other fines incurred during business travel.
 First-class airfare under any circumstance without CFO pre-approval.
7. Audit and Non-Compliance

 Traffic violations, parking tickets, or other fines incurred during business travel.
 First-class airfare under any circumstance without CFO pre-approval.
7. Audit and Non-Compliance
Finance conducts quarterly random audits of expense reports. Employees found submitting fraudulent or
materially inaccurate expense claims are subject to disciplinary action up to and including termination, and
Finance reserves the right to claw back reimbursed amounts through payroll deduction where permitted by
local law.
This document is classified Internal Use Only. For questions, contact Finance Operations at
financeops@acmecorp-internal.example.

Acme Corporation
 Human Resources — Remote Work & Home Office Equipment Policy
Document ID: ACME-POL-HR-007  |  Version: 2.1  |  Effective Date: March 3, 2026  |  Classification: Internal Use Only
1. Purpose
This policy defines eligibility, expectations, and equipment support for employees who work remotely on a
full-time, hybrid, or occasional basis. It is administered by Human Resources in coordination with the IT
Helpdesk and People Managers.
2. Eligibility and Work Arrangements
Employees may request one of three arrangements, subject to manager approval: Fully Remote (no
regular office attendance required), Hybrid (minimum 2 days per week in an Acme office), or Office-Based
(5 days per week on-site). Remote work eligibility is reviewed at the start of each fiscal year and may be
revoked if role requirements change.
3. Core Working Hours and Availability
Remote and hybrid employees must be reachable via Slack and calendar during their team's designated

revoked if role requirements change.
3. Core Working Hours and Availability
Remote and hybrid employees must be reachable via Slack and calendar during their team's designated
core hours, typically 10:00 AM to 3:00 PM local time, regardless of arrangement. Employees working
across time zones from their team should agree on an overlap window with their manager in writing.
4. Home Office Equipment and Stipend
Acme provides a one-time home office setup stipend of $750 for newly remote or hybrid employees,
covering desks, chairs, and monitors. In addition, employees receive an ongoing monthly remote work
stipend of $85 to offset internet and utility costs. Stipend requests are submitted through the Workday
Expense module under category 'Remote Equipment.'
 Company-issued laptop, keyboard, and mouse remain Acme property and must be returned upon
separation.
 Employees are responsible for maintaining a private, secure internet connection with a minimum of
25 Mbps download speed.

 Employees are responsible for maintaining a private, secure internet connection with a minimum of
25 Mbps download speed.
 Personal printers, webcams, and headsets are eligible for stipend reimbursement up to $150
combined per calendar year.
5. Remote Work and Network Security Requirements
Employees working outside an Acme office must connect to company systems using the
company-approved VPN client at all times when accessing internal applications. Use of public Wi-Fi

(cafes, airports, hotels) for company business is discouraged; if unavoidable, VPN connection is
mandatory before accessing any internal system. Employees must not use personal, unmanaged devices
to access Confidential or Restricted data as defined in the IT Security Policy (ACME-POL-IT-014).
6. International Remote Work
Employees relocating to work from a country other than their country of employment record must receive
prior written approval from HR and Legal at least 30 days in advance, due to tax, payroll, and employment
law implications. Unapproved international remote work may result in suspension of system access and
disciplinary review.
7. Performance and Check-ins
Managers of remote and hybrid employees are expected to conduct at least one 1:1 check-in per week
and a documented quarterly performance conversation. Remote employees are held to the same
performance standards, promotion criteria, and review cycles as office-based employees; remote status

and a documented quarterly performance conversation. Remote employees are held to the same
performance standards, promotion criteria, and review cycles as office-based employees; remote status
must never be a factor in performance ratings.

Acme Corporation
 Information Technology Security & Acceptable Use Policy
 Document ID: ACME-POL-IT-014  |  Version: 3.2  |  Effective Date: January 15, 2026  |  Classification: Internal Use
 Only
1. Purpose and Scope
This policy establishes the minimum security standards and acceptable use requirements for all
employees, contractors, and third-party vendors who access Acme Corporation's information systems,
networks, and data. It applies to all company-owned and personally owned devices used to conduct
company business, whether on-premises, remote, or hybrid.
This document is reviewed annually by the Information Security Office and supersedes all previous
versions upon publication. Employees are required to acknowledge this policy during onboarding and upon
each material revision.
2. Password and Authentication Requirements
All employees must comply with the following authentication standards when accessing Acme systems:

each material revision.
2. Password and Authentication Requirements
All employees must comply with the following authentication standards when accessing Acme systems:
 Passwords must be a minimum of 14 characters and include at least one uppercase letter, one
lowercase letter, one number, and one special character.
 Multi-factor authentication (MFA) is mandatory for all remote access, VPN connections, and cloud
application logins (Okta, Google Workspace, AWS Console).
 Passwords must not be reused across the last 10 password cycles.
 Shared or generic accounts are prohibited except where explicitly approved by the Information
Security Office for service accounts.
 Employees must report suspected credential compromise to the Security Operations Center (SOC)
within 1 hour of discovery.
3. Data Classification Standards
All company data must be classified according to the following tiers. Handling, storage, and transmission

4. Acceptable Use of Company Systems
Company systems, including laptops, mobile devices, email, and cloud storage, are provided for business
purposes. Limited personal use is permitted provided it does not interfere with job performance, consume
excessive resources, or violate any provision of this policy.
4.1 Prohibited Activities
 Installing unauthorized software or browser extensions on company-managed devices.
 Transmitting Confidential or Restricted data to personal email accounts or unapproved cloud storage
services.
 Disabling or circumventing endpoint security agents, VPN clients, or device management profiles.
 Using company systems to access, store, or distribute unlicensed or infringing content.
 Connecting unapproved USB storage devices to systems that process Restricted data.
5. Incident Reporting and Response

 Connecting unapproved USB storage devices to systems that process Restricted data.
5. Incident Reporting and Response
Any suspected security incident, including phishing attempts, malware infections, lost or stolen devices, or
unauthorized access, must be reported immediately to the Security Operations Center at
soc@acmecorp-internal.example or via the internal Incident Portal. Do not attempt to independently
investigate or remediate a suspected breach.
Target response times are as follows: Critical incidents (active data exfiltration, ransomware) — 15
minutes; High severity (confirmed malware, account compromise) — 1 hour; Medium severity (policy
violations, suspicious activity) — 4 business hours; Low severity (informational reports) — 2 business
days.
6. Remote Work and Device Security
Employees working remotely must connect to company systems exclusively through the approved VPN

days.
6. Remote Work and Device Security
Employees working remotely must connect to company systems exclusively through the approved VPN
client and must not use public, unsecured Wi-Fi networks to access Confidential or Restricted data without
VPN protection. All company-issued laptops must have full-disk encryption, endpoint detection and
response (EDR) software, and automatic screen locking after 5 minutes of inactivity enabled at all times.

7. Roles and Responsibilities
Role
Responsibility
Chief Information Security Officer (CISO)
Owns this policy; approves annual revisions and exceptions
Security Operations Center (SOC)
Monitors, triages, and responds to security incidents 24/7
IT Helpdesk
Provisions accounts, enforces MFA enrollment, manages device compliance
People Managers
Ensure direct reports complete annual security training and policy acknowledgment
All Employees
Comply with this policy and report suspected incidents promptly
8. Enforcement and Exceptions
Violations of this policy may result in disciplinary action up to and including termination of employment or
contract, and may be reported to law enforcement where required by law. Exceptions to this policy must be
requested in writing to the Information Security Office and are granted only for a defined period with
compensating controls documented.
